text: {"frames":["Olive opened the last glass jar on the market shelf and found it empty, though it had held a dream of a schoolroom the night before. A small paper tag was tied to the neck, with the name of the room written in careful pencil. The dream had been packed to fit exactly into that room, and now it was lost somewhere in the Tower's crooked halls. Olive knew that a dream needs room to rest, so she would have to find the right amount of floor to search. Which guess do you choose for the floor of that classroom, in square metres?","Briony heard a knock at the lock gate, though no boat was in sight. A letter floated up on the water, folded like a small paper boat, and her candle in the lock house flickered in its reflection. The writer begged for help, because the schoolroom on the third floor had lost its lamp and the children could not see the chalk. Briony had to tell the caretaker how big the floor was, so the new lamp could be sent up the right canal. Which guess do you choose for the floor of that classroom, in square metres?","Before dawn the ice on the Tower canal was marked with wet footprints, and they went in a small circle and then stopped at a door. A smell of warm bread and chalk came from under it. Inside, a row of wooden clogs had been lined up along the wall, each one with a tiny chalk mark. The footprints had been counted in the night, and someone wanted to know how much floor there was to walk on. Which guess do you choose for the floor of that classroom, in square metres?","Teun the traveller had no shadow, and the silent watchman at the dyke gate had stopped to look at it. Teun pointed at the stone where his shadow should have been and said nothing. The watchman, who had never been seen by day, took out a rope and began to pace the flagstones of the schoolroom beneath the dyke. He wanted to know how much floor the schoolroom had, so the lost shadow could be folded and laid down in the right place. Which guess do you choose for the floor of that classroom, in square metres?","Flora the stork landed on the windowsill with a voice in her beak, counting steps through the fog. She was counting for someone who lived in the Tower, and she could not reach the top floor. The stork was sure that the lost voice had been left in a room with plain wooden benches and a stove in the corner. To send the voice home by the right chimney, Flora needed to know how much floor the room covered. Which guess do you choose for the floor of that classroom, in square metres?"]}
